fields.purpose: inventory purchases and long-term supply and capacity obligations for Hopper and Blackwell
fields.verbatim_quote: As of July 28, 2024, we had outstanding inventory purchases and long-term supply and capacity obligations totaling $27.8 billion, an increase from the prior year due to commitments for Hopper and Blackwell capacity and components.

fields.purpose: multi-year cloud service agreements for R&D and DGX Cloud
fields.verbatim_quote: Other non-inventory purchase obligations were $12.0 billion, including $9.8 billion of multi-year cloud service agreements. We expect our cloud service agreements to be used to support our research and development efforts and our DGX Cloud offerings.

fields.purpose: data center leases expected to commence
fields.verbatim_quote: In addition, operating leases of $1.0 billion, primarily for our data centers, are expected to commence during fiscal year 2025 with lease terms of 2 to 10.5 years.

In October 2023, the USG announced new and updated licensing requirements that became effective in our fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024 for exports to China and Country Groups D1, D4, and D5 (including but not limited to Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Vietnam, but excluding Israel) of our products exceeding certain performance thresholds, including A100, A800, H100, H800, L4, L40, L40S and RTX 4090.

numeric_signal.note: Total future purchase commitments through 2030 and beyond

fields.verbatim_quote: Total future purchase commitments as of July 28, 2024 are as follows: ... Total $39,781 million. We continue to increase our supply and capacity purchases with existing and new suppliers to support our demand projections.

We executed a change to the Blackwell GPU mask to improve production yield. Blackwell production ramp is scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter and continue into fiscal year 2026. In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, we expect to ship several billion dollars in Blackwell revenue.

Sales to direct Customers, A, B, C and D represented 14%, 11%, 11% and 10% of total revenue, respectively, for the second quarter of fiscal year 2025, all of which were primarily attributable to the Compute & Networking segment.

Provisions for inventory and excess inventory purchase obligations totaled $908 million and $1.3 billion for the second quarter and first half of fiscal year 2025, respectively, and were primarily due to low-yielding Blackwell material.

[chunk 2/2] NVIDIA 10-Q filing (2024-08-28) – Focus on SIFI-material entities and risks. Key findings:

1. **CAPEX_ROI_GAP (Severity 3)**: $39.8B in total future purchase commitments through FY2030, with significant concentration in Hopper and Blackwell capacity. Strong sequential revenue growth (122% YoY) but large inventory provisions ($1.3B in H1 FY2025 for low-yielding Blackwell) indicate execution risk on new product transitions.

2. **EXECUTION_RISK-Blackwell (Severity 3)**: Blackwell production ramp delayed; mask change needed to improve yield. Already incurring material inventory provisions. "Fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, we expect to ship several billion dollars in Blackwell revenue" – timing execution risk on a major transition.

3. **CUSTOMER_CONCENTRATION (Severity 3)**: Top 5 direct customers (A, B, C, D, E) represent 14%, 11%, 11%, 10%, and 10% of revenue. Two indirect customers (through B and E) also ~10% each. Highly concentrated customer base in Compute & Networking segment (88% of revenue). "Many end customers often do not purchase directly from us but purchase indirectly through multiple OEMs, ODMs, system integrators, distributors."

4. **COST_OPACITY (Severity 3)**: $1.3B inventory provisions in H1 FY2025 (2.3% of reported revenue) – primarily low-yielding Blackwell. Gross margin impact of -2.0% to -2.7% from provisions. Hidden complexity in supply chain adjustments and prepaid capacity agreements ($3.3B + $1.3B current/long-term).

5. **EXPORT CONTROL RISK (Severity 4)**: Critical geopolitical dependency on Taiwan supply and USG licensing. Cannot ship A100/H100/restricted chips to China without license (none granted). China is significant market (~6% of total revenue, but Data Center revenue "grew sequentially in the second quarter... and is a significant contributor"). Mitigation: developed China-specific products not requiring licenses, but noted these represent lower-margin products.

6. **SUPPLIER_CONCENTRATION**: Reliance on Taiwan (TSMC, etc.). "Our business depends on our ability to receive consistent and reliable supply from our overseas partners, especially in Taiwan." Geopolitical risk flagged but not quantified.

No off-balance-sheet entities, SPVs, or VIEs detected in this filing section. No private AI lab investments disclosed in the narrative sections examined (Note 8 on investments referenced but not reproduced in source text). No evidence of circular revenue relationships or round-tripping detected.
